videos.title: AI Safety Fact vs. Fiction | YC Paper Club
videos.description:
This week’s Paper Club is all about AI safety - not the headlines, the science. AI safety has been a research field for decades, with its own conferences, methods, and a track record in systems like aircraft collision avoidance, where the standard is one catastrophic failure per billion flight hours.

In this episode we'll hear from Clark Barrett and Mykel Kochenderfer, Stanford professors and co-directors of the Stanford Center for AI Safety.  Together with Francois they'll discuss what actually happened in the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident versus what got reported, how automated reasoning can mathematically prove that code cannot be hacked, how the stress-testing methods built to validate aircraft are now being turned on language models, and why we might need an NTSB for AI.

Join us for the next Paper Club on October 21st, where we'll talk Inference: https://events.ycombinator.com/yc-paperclub-oct21

Chapters:
00:00 - Science fiction vs. science fact
04:32 - Engineering problem, or P(doom)
06:04 - What actually happened at Hugging Face
07:53 - Where "10% in 10 years" comes from

17:25 - Clark Barrett: when AI met automated reasoning

videos.title: Dating Coach: The Signs He'll Never Commit to You | Sabrina Zohar
videos.description:
You’ve heard “if he wanted to, he would.” Sabrina Zohar says that line is keeping you single.

In this clip, Sabrina Zohar and Jay Shetty talk about why we chase people who don’t choose us. Sabrina shares the two questions that changed how she dates. And she explains why the person who feels most familiar is often the wrong one.

She shares the first-date question that shows red flags fast, and she talks about why butterflies aren’t always a good sign. She also opens up about what she told her partner at the end of their very first date.

Learn why someone can be perfect for six weeks and then suddenly pull away. And learn why “right person, wrong time” might be a story we tell ourselves.
